concepts.title: Cell Signaling: Paracrine Autocrine and Endocrine
concepts.definition: Cells converse through chemical messengers that only work where a matching receptor waits: short-range release reaching neighbours at once is paracrine, a cell talking back to its own receptors is autocrine - the trick cancer cells abuse by making their own growth factors - and hormones riding the bloodstream to distant targets is endocrine signaling.
concepts.key_idea: Distance decides the name of the signaling; no receptor on the cell means no response, whatever the ligand level.
question_patterns: differentiate paracrine autocrine and endocrine signaling with one example of each
why do cancer cells not depend on outside growth factors - name the signaling they exploit
what is a ligand and why must its receptor be specific for the message to work
where may a receptor sit inside or on a cell - list the three possible locations
neuronal communication is an example of which signaling type - justify
what happens inside a cell once a ligand locks onto its receptor

solution_steps.explain: Neighbour-close release is paracrine, self-stimulation is autocrine, blood-borne travel to far targets is endocrine.
A response requires the corresponding receptor on the surface, in the cytoplasm or in the nucleus.
Binding deforms the receptor and starts the message relay that changes cell activities.

worked_examples.q: Short-range messengers reaching neighbours at once is what signalling: paracrine or endocrine?

concepts.title: Glycolysis and the Fate of Pyruvate
concepts.definition: In the cytosol the Embden-Meyerhof-Parnas route splits one six-carbon glucose into two three-carbon pyruvates over ten enzyme steps, spending two ATP early and banking four later, with hexokinase, phosphofructokinase and pyruvate kinase marking the three irreversible control points; afterwards pyruvate either becomes lactate or ethanol without air, or enters mitochondria as acetyl CoA when oxygen is present.
concepts.key_idea: Three regulated, irreversible enzymes steer glycolysis, and oxygen availability alone picks pyruvate's next destination.
question_patterns: list the ten enzymatic steps of glycolysis naming the enzyme at each step
which three glycolytic reactions are irreversible and why are they called regulatory
what are the two anaerobic fates and the one aerobic fate of pyruvate
which enzyme links glycolysis to the citric acid cycle and where is it located
why must NADH be reoxidised to NAD+ for glycolysis to keep running
name the coenzyme of pyruvate decarboxylase and the two enzymes of alcoholic fermentation
how does the aldolase reaction split fructose-1-6-bisphosphate and which trioses appear

solution_steps.explain: Glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, fructose-1-6-bisphosphate, then aldolase cleavage into two triose phosphates that converge on pyruvate.
Hexokinase, phosphofructokinase and pyruvate kinase each run an irreversible, allosterically regulated step.
No oxygen: lactate via lactate dehydrogenase or ethanol via decarboxylase plus dehydrogenase; oxygen present: acetyl CoA via the PDH complex.

worked_examples.q: The two pyruvates from one glucose carry how many carbon atoms together?

concepts.title: Energy Yield of Glycolysis and Fermentation
concepts.definition: Each glucose passing down the glycolytic line returns four ATP at the two substrate-level phosphorylation steps - two per triose across the two trioses formed - while two ATP were spent priming the sugar, so the net harvest is two; fermentation extends this by recycling NAD+ yet still yields only two ATP per glucose.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract the two priming ATP from the four collected to get the net two per glucose.
concepts.textbook_ref: kebt105.txt section 5.2.4 Energy yield by glycolysis
question_patterns: compute the net ATP gain of glycolysis given that four ATP are generated and two are consumed
how many ATP does one glucose yield under homolactic fermentation and why so low
write the balanced net equation of glycolysis showing ATP ADP NAD+ and NADH terms
at which two enzymatic steps does substrate-level phosphorylation bank ATP in glycolysis
why does the per-triose ATP gain double when counted per glucose
compare the ATP return of alcoholic fermentation with that of aerobic oxidation of pyruvate

solution_steps.explain: Each triose pays two ATP at phosphoglycerate kinase and pyruvate kinase; two trioses arise per glucose.
Hexokinase and phosphofructokinase each spent one ATP, so subtract the investment.

worked_examples.q: What is the net ATP yield of glycolysis per glucose?

concepts.title: Citric Acid Cycle in the Mitochondrial Matrix
concepts.definition: Hans Kreb's cycle condenses a two-carbon acetyl group with four-carbon oxaloacetate into citrate and walks it through decarboxylations and dehydrogenations back to oxaloacetate, banking three NADH, one FADH2 and one GTP per turn; all its enzymes sit in the mitochondrial matrix except succinate dehydrogenase, which alone is embedded in the inner membrane.
concepts.key_idea: One turn burns one acetyl group to two CO2 while loading three NADH, one FADH2 and one GTP.
question_patterns: write the overall equation of the citric acid cycle for one acetyl CoA
which enzyme of the TCA cycle remains attached to the inner mitochondrial membrane and what cofactors does it carry
at which single step does substrate-level phosphorylation occur in the cycle - name the enzyme and product
name the two decarboxylation steps of the cycle and the enzymes catalysing them
why is the citric acid cycle called the final common pathway of carbohydrate lipid and protein oxidation
how many isozyme forms does isocitrate dehydrogenase show and which coenzyme does each prefer

solution_steps.explain: Citrate synthase joins acetyl CoA to oxaloacetate forming citrate; aconitase shifts it to isocitrate.
Two NAD+-linked decarboxylations release two CO2 and produce succinyl CoA via alpha-ketoglutarate.
Succinyl CoA synthetase banks GTP, succinate dehydrogenase loads FADH2, and malate dehydrogenase restores oxaloacetate with a third NADH.

worked_examples.q: Which cycle condenses an acetyl group with oxaloacetate: the citric acid cycle or glycolysis?

concepts.title: Electron Transport Chain and Oxidative Phosphorylation
concepts.definition: Four giant complexes in the inner mitochondrial membrane pass electrons from NADH and FADH2 down to oxygen, pumping protons as complexes I, III and IV work - enough gradient for about 1, 0.5 and 1 ATP respectively - so one matrix NADH finally buys about 2.5 ATP while FADH2, entering at QH2 past complex I, buys only about 1.5.
concepts.key_idea: Price NADH at 2.5 ATP and FADH2 at 1.5 ATP; complex II feeds in later and so pays less.
question_patterns: mitochondria oxidise 10 NADH and 4 FADH2 - how many ATP does oxidative phosphorylation deliver in total
why does FADH2 yield fewer ATP than NADH - answer with the entry point of its electrons
name the four complexes of the electron transport chain and state which ones pump protons
what is the proton motive force and how does ATP synthase exploit it
which molecule accepts electrons at the end of the chain and what product appears
how many ATP correspond to the gradients built by complexes I III and IV individually

solution_steps.explain: Each matrix NADH drives complexes I, III and IV for about 2.5 ATP.
Electrons entering at QH2 skip complex I, so each FADH2 earns about 1.5 ATP.
The sum is the total ATP delivered by oxidative phosphorylation.

worked_examples.q: One matrix NADH buys about how many ATP: 2.5 or 25?

concepts.title: Photosynthesis Light Reactions and Calvin Cycle
concepts.definition: Chloroplast machinery runs two phases: photosystems II and I split water - two molecules give one oxygen for every four electrons shipped to PSI - and build ATP plus NADPH by photophosphorylation, while the Calvin cycle in the stroma spends those coins to fix carbon dioxide onto ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate, reducing the six formed 3-phosphoglycerates with six ATP and six NADPH and then paying three more ATP to regenerate the acceptor.
concepts.key_idea: Fixing three CO2 makes six 3-phosphoglycerate, so the reduction bill is six ATP plus six NADPH with three ATP more for regeneration.
question_patterns: for every four electrons sent from PSII to PSI how many water molecules are split and how much oxygen evolves
how many ATP and NADPH does the Calvin cycle consume to fix three molecules of CO2
name the enzyme that fixes CO2 in the Calvin cycle and state its two activities
differentiate cyclic from non-cyclic photophosphorylation in terms of products
at which wavelengths do PSI and PSII respond - give the nanometre values
why is the Calvin cycle called the C3 cycle and where do its reactions occur
how does the C4 pathway of maize differ from the C3 pathway in its first CO2 acceptor

solution_steps.explain: Each CO2 fixed on ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate yields two 3-phosphoglycerate molecules.
Reducing the PGA takes one ATP per molecule; regenerating the acceptor adds three more ATP per three CO2.
Four electrons pulled from water accompany two water molecules split into one O2.

worked_examples.q: Which cycle fixes carbon dioxide onto ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate: the Calvin cycle or the Krebs cycle?

concepts.title: Cell Cycle Arithmetic and Mitotic Stages
concepts.definition: A dividing cell passes through G1 growth, S phase where the 2C DNA content doubles to 4C, G2 preparation, and then mitosis - prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase - followed by cytokinesis; because every round doubles the population, starting from one cell, r rounds leave two raised to r cells and one fewer division events than cells produced.
concepts.key_idea: Two raised to the number of rounds sizes a clone; subtract the starting cell to count the divisions performed.
question_patterns: how many mitotic rounds take a single cell to 64 cells and how many total divisions is that
a culture starts from 4 cells and doubles three times - how many cells and how many division events result
what happens to the DNA content of a cell during S phase - express the change from 2C
list the four stages of karyokinesis with one landmark event of each
which structure anchors chromosomes to spindle fibers and where does it sit
how does cytokinesis differ between an animal cell and a plant cell

solution_steps.explain: Each mitotic round doubles the cell count, so raise two to the round count.
Every new cell beyond the starters needed one division, so subtract the founders.

worked_examples.q: Starting from one cell, how many cells do 3 rounds of division leave?

concepts.title: Meiosis, Apoptosis, Stem Cells and Migration
concepts.definition: Two reductions shape cell life: meiosis halves the chromosome set across a reductional first division and an equational second one, delivering four haploid cells enriched by crossing over at pachytene; apoptosis then prunes unneeded cells by programmed DNA fragmentation and membrane blebbing without inflammation, unlike traumatic necrosis; meanwhile stem cells of totipotent, pluripotent or multipotent grade repair tissues, and cell migration walks single cells or sheets through embryogenesis, wound healing and cancer spread.
concepts.key_idea: Halving, pruning, specialising and moving - the four long-term acts that shape a multicellular organism.
question_patterns: give a comparative account of apoptosis and necrosis
name the five substages of prophase I and the event that defines pachytene
why is meiosis I called reductional while meiosis II is equational
differentiate totipotent pluripotent and multipotent stem cells with one example of each
what makes a bivalent and at which zygotene structure does synapsis occur
list the four steps of cell migration in order from protrusion to rear retraction
how does cell migration assist gastrulation and what danger does metastasis pose

solution_steps.explain: One interphase then two nuclear divisions; homologues part in anaphase I, sister chromatids in anaphase II.
Apoptosis is ordered, energy-dependent and silently phagocytosed; necrosis spills contents and inflames.
Totipotent cells build everything including extraembryonic tissue, pluripotent build the three germ layers, multipotent only a narrow set such as blood cells.

worked_examples.q: Which division halves the chromosome set: meiosis or mitosis?

worked_examples.question_pattern: The Calvin cycle fixes {co2_fixed} molecules of CO2. Find the 3-phosphoglycerate molecules formed, the ATP bill for their reduction plus acceptor regeneration, and the NADPH consumed.

extracted_variables.co2_fixed: molecules of CO2 fixed in the cycle

solution_template.explain: One ATP per PGA for reduction plus three ATP for regeneration of RuBP.
Reduction of each PGA consumes one NADPH.

worked_examples.source_ref: kebt105.txt section 5.3.1 and Exercise 3 (64 cells from one cell)
worked_examples.question_pattern: A culture is started from {initial_cells} cell(s) and allowed {rounds} mitotic rounds. Find the final cell count and the total number of division events performed.

solution_template.explain: Two raised to the rounds multiplies the founders.
Each cell beyond the founders costs one division.
